title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
prompt:
A path is any sequence of connected nodes (each adjacent pair shares an edge); it need not pass through the root. Return the maximum sum of node values along any path.

**Example**: `[-10,9,20,null,null,15,7]` → `42` (15 → 20 → 7).

DFS returns the best downward 'arm' from each node; a shared best considers the full path that bends through the node (left arm + node + right arm).

tests.note: a single negative node — must take it

hints: Helper returns the best sum of a path going DOWN from a node (node + one child arm), clamping negatives to 0.
At each node, the best path bending here is `node.val + leftArm + rightArm` — update the shared best with it.
Return `node.val + max(leftArm, rightArm)` upward (you can only extend one arm to the parent).

solution.explanation: O(n). Two distinct quantities again: the full through-node path (recorded in `best`) can use both arms, but the value returned to the parent can use only one (a path can't fork). Clamping negative arms to 0 means 'don't include this subtree if it only subtracts' — except the node itself, which is always taken, handling all-negative trees.
